_README: ENGLISH LEAD-INS FOR FIELD KEYS THAT REACH READER-FACING PROSE.
Mahmood's decision, 2026-08-23: field names get a proper English lead-in rather than a
refusal. The prior state put schema identifiers in sentences -- 'what verifies this
object: ClinicalTrials.gov protocol records, read 2026-08-18. bar: not recorded on the
page this object was built from.' -- which reads as a data structure with its punctuation
THE GOVERNING CONSTRAINT: A LEAD-IN MUST NOT ASSERT MORE THAN THE FIELD HOLDS.
`what_verifies_this_object` becomes 'This object's verification rests on X', which is the
field's own claim in English. It must NOT become 'the data were verified', which asserts
TWO FORMS PER KEY, BECAUSE MOST VALUES ARE NULL MARKERS. 35 of 39 `bar` values read 'not
recorded on the page this object was extracted from'. A single template would produce
'The bar for verification was: not recorded on the page this object was extracted from',
which is a sentence about nothing. `absent` is used when the value is a null marker, and
it states the ABSENCE as the fact -- the house rule that a stated absence is a decision
and an omitted field reads as an oversight.
KEYS THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER are listed in `_refused` with the reason. A
fluent wrong sentence is worse than a visible field name: a field name is obviously
unfinished, and a wrong lead-in is not.

what_verifies_this_object.absent: The basis on which this object was verified is not recorded.
what_verifies_this_object.note: The field names what the verification rests on. It does not record that any check was performed, so the lead-in says 'rests on' and not 'was verified against'.

what_is_not_claimed.absent: What this object does not claim is not recorded.
what_is_not_claimed.note: A LIMITATION, AND THE LEAD-IN MUST KEEP IT ONE. Values begin 'that ...', so 'This review does not claim that any per-trial count was checked against a results record' is a plain statement that the check was not done. It is deliberately not softened to 'it should be noted that' or any caveat form.

bar.present: The bar this object had to clear was: %s
bar.absent: The bar this object had to clear is not recorded.
bar.note: `verification_basis.bar` is the threshold for verification. Its one populated form reads 'Both families must find no defect in the object. A finding about the validator is not a finding about the object and does not block.' -- a criterion, so the lead-in names it as one.

post_hoc.present: The eligibility criteria were derived after the review was carried out rather than specified in advance.
post_hoc.absent: Whether the eligibility criteria were specified in advance is not recorded.
post_hoc.note: `screening.eligibility_provenance.post_hoc` is a BOOLEAN and its value is not the sentence -- the KEY is the claim. Rendered only when true; when false the sibling `predefined` carries the positive statement. Value is ignored by the renderer for this key.

cascade_steps._note: Names of the sources checked in `inputs.trials[].by_outcome.<oid>.cascade.checked`. Confirmed against `source_tier`, which takes the values 'registry' and 'primary_oa'.

_refused.families: REFUSED BY NAME, 8 occurrences, and listed for Mahmood rather than guessed. The key appears under TWO containers with two different meanings -- `verification_basis.families` (a list, usually empty) and `screening.duplicate_screening.families` (a mapping of screener to vendor, e.g. codex -> openai, agy -> google). Both are sayable in English; which one a given rendered occurrence came from is NOT recoverable from the flattened text, and a lead-in naming the wrong one would be a fluent false statement about how the review was screened. Needs a decision per container, or a renderer that carries the path.
